title: RECOVER-TLC Semaglutide Treatment Trial
official: Tame-LC: A Phase 2b Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Trial Designed to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of a 6-month Course of Semaglutide in Individuals Aged 12-70 Years With Long COVID
summary: The Tame-LC trial is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase IIb trial designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of semaglutide administered subcutaneously once-weekly for improvement of overall Health-related Quality of Life (HRQoL) and select symptoms in adolescents and adults aged 12 to 70 years with Long COVID. A total of 774 participants (642 adults and 132 adolescents) will be randomized in a 2:2:1:1 allocation ratio to receive semaglutide up to 1.0 mg (maximum tolerated dose), semaglutide up to 2.4 mg (maximum tolerated dose), placebo up to 1.0 mg, or placebo up to 2.4 mg. The trial involves a combination of patient-reported outcomes (PROs), other assessments (e.g., cognitive tests, 6-minute walk test), and blood biomarkers that may be useful for tracking improvement (e.g., inflammatory, immunologic, neurologic, cardiovascular, and metabolic biomarkers. Semaglutide is expected to provide clinical benefits to a wide array of symptoms regardless of weight loss. Therefore, the study will evaluate improvements in HRQoL but also specific clinical features of Long COVID, including fatigue, cognitive difficulties, dysautonomia, and post-exertional malaise (PEM), in treatment versus placebo arms. In addition, it will evaluate the specific doses at which benefits are observed via randomization of participants to one of two dosing arms. Durability of improvement will be evaluated 3 months after cessation of study product. The primary objective is to evaluate the effect of a 6-month course of semaglutide compared to placebo on the change in overall HRQoL from baseline to 6 months after randomization among participants aged 18-70 years with Long COVID.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1\. Individuals aged 12-70 years inclusive at randomization. 2. Fluent in English or Spanish. 3. History of SARS-CoV 2 infection,\* shown by (1) a positive nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) or antigen test, OR (2) meeting clinical criteria\*\* AND an epidemiologic link\* to a confirmed case.

\*Visit 00 for a list of acceptable documentation required to confirm past SARS-CoV 2 infection.

\*\*Clinical criteria are defined as either (1) acute onset of fever AND cough; OR (2) acute altered/loss of taste or smell + one additional symptom including fever, cough, general weakness/fatigue, headache, myalgia, sore throat, coryza, dyspnea, nausea, diarrhea, or anorexia; OR (3) three or more symptoms including fever, cough, general weakness/fatigue, headache, myalgia, sore throat, coryza, dyspnea, nausea, diarrhea, or anorexia.

* Epidemiologic link is defined as having contact (within 6 feet for at least 15 minutes) with someone sick with SARS-CoV 2 test-positive COVID 19 illness.

  4\. Clinical evidence of Long COVID\* and Long COVID symptoms that cannot be attributed to another cause upon investigator review of medical history and workup participant received prior to study entry.

  \*Participants must meet the 2024 National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine definition for Long COVID.

  5\. Impairment\*, \*\* in ability to engage in pre-Long COVID levels of activity that began during or in the 6 months following the onset of the qualifying SARS-CoV infection (see inclusion criterion #3).

  \*Level of impairment can fluctuate but (i) the total duration of impairment must be at least 3 months at time of randomization and (ii) impairment must be present for more days than not in the 30 days prior to randomization.
  * For this trial, impairment may include occupational, educational, social, or personal aspects of one's life.

    6\. Has at least two new symptoms/syndromes\*, \*\* that began either during or in the 6 months following the onset of the qualifying SARS-CoV 2 infection (see inclusion criterion #2).
    * At least one of the symptoms/syndromes must be present for at least 3 months and be present at randomization even if it fluctuates in quality over time.
  * List of qualifying new symptoms/syndromes include the following:

    1. Fatigue-A persistent state of physical or mental exhaustion that is not substantially alleviated by sleep or rest that interferes with normal functioning, is often profound, and is not the result of ongoing or unusual excessive exertion. Defined by a previous clinical diagnosis, a score of =35 on the Fatigue Severity Scale (participants aged 18-70), or a score of \<70 on the Pediatric Quality of Life Multidimensional Fatigue Scale \[PedsQL-MFS\] (participants aged 12-17) at Visit 00. 7. Participant with PROMIS-Preference (PROPr) score of = 0.40 on the (Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System) PROMIS-29+2 (participants aged 18-70) or a score of \<76 on the PedsQL Generic Core Scales Short Form\* 15 (participants aged 12-17) at Visit 00.

       8\. Willing and able to provide informed consent and assent (as applicable) before initiation of any study procedures 9. Able to understand and agree to complete the intervention, comply with all planned study procedures (e.g., assessments\*), and be available for all study visits.

       \*Some assessments may require parent or legal guardian completion. 10.Agrees to utilize electronic data capture for the e-Memory Aid and electronic Patient-Reported Outcome (PROs).

       Exclusion Criteria:
       1. Known acute SARS-CoV 2 infection = 30 days before randomization.
       2. Has Type 1 diabetes or has current or recent (i.e., within 7 days of informed consent) use of sulfonylureas, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP 4) inhibitor (gliptins), meglitinides (glinides), or insulin.
       3. HbA1c \> 7.0 percent at Visit 00\*.

          * A repeat HbA1c may be performed at the investigator's discretion only if the screening result is inconsistent with the participant's clinical history.
       4. Current or recent use of a GLP 1 RA within 8 weeks of informed consent (regardless of reason for use).
       5. Use of a GLP 1 RA to treat Long COVID for \>/= 8 weeks duration in the 6 months before informed consent
       6. Known allergy/sensitivity/hypersensitivity to study product or its components.
       7. Positive pregnancy test at Visit 00/Visit 01 or within 24 hours before study product administration
       8. Plans to become pregnant during the trial period (including 2 months after cessation of study product) or is breastfeeding at randomization
       9. Is of child-bearing potential and not using a highly effective contraceptive method.
       10. Screening laboratory tests that are \> Grade 1 per Division of AIDS (DAIDS) v2.1 Toxicity Table.
       11. Participation in another interventional clinical trial within 30 days of informed consent or planned participation during trial period.
       12. Began a new medication, supplement, or vitamin, or changed doses of a medication, supplement, or vitamin within 30 days of informed consent.
       13. Has recent active malignancy (received chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the 12 months prior to randomization) or current active malignancy at randomization\*.

           * COVID patients with non-melanoma skin carcinoma (basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer), or low-grade cervical squamous intraepithelial lesions, which are considered cured and not requiring ongoing therapy, may be enrolled at the discretion of the investigator.
       14. Has known active Hepatitis B (HBV) infection, active Hepatitis C (HCV) infection, or unstable/untreated\*Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection.
       15. BMI \<20 kg/m\^2 for adults (age 18-70 years) or the 25th percentile based on CDC BMI for age by sex threshold for adolescents (aged 12-17 years).
       16. Personal or first-degree relative(s) history of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Syndrome Type 2(MEN 2) or Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma (MTC).
       17. Presence of medically diagnosed gastroparesis, that is active at the time of randomization.
       18. Evidence of pre-renal azotemia per clinical judgment at randomization, after assessing combination of laboratory results, vital signs, and physical exam findings.
       19. Current or past history of any of the following: recurrent hypoglycemia, medical condition involving the pancreas, gallbladder, eye or kidney\*.

           * Conditions include but not limited to pancreatitis, cholecystitis, cholelithiasis, diabetic retinopathy, severe chronic kidney disease and/or chronic kidney failure (eGFR \<30 mm/min/1.73 m\^2).
       20. Plans to have elective surgery or procedure which may involve general anesthesia or deep sedation during the study intervention.
       21. Person with clinical diagnosis of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS), autonomic dysfunction, or other infection-associated chronic conditions with an onset prior to the qualifying SARS-CoV 2 infection or COVID 19 illness.
       22. Has a history of a clinically significant mental health condition\*, \*\*, \*\*\*. \*History of prior suicide attempt.
  * Hospitalized in the 6 months prior to randomization for mental health symptoms or worsening of a known mental health condition.
* Has a moderate or high-risk score on C-SSRS at Visit 00. 23. Indication of opioid or alcohol use disorder in individuals 18 and older based on 1) self-report about the preceding 1 year before enrollment, 2) documentation in medical records, or 3) positive screening suggesting a potential problem with alcohol or opioids\*\*.

  * Score \>/= 8i on the self-administered full AUDIT i. Adults aged \>/=18 years, an alcohol use screen will be conducted using the AUDIT-C. Participants with an AUDIT-C score \>/=3 (females) or \>/=4 (males) will complete the full AUDIT. A score \>/=8 on the full AUDIT assessment (regardless of sex) constitutes a positive alcohol use screen.

    b. Positive urine toxicology test for opioid use at the screening visit. A positive screening suggesting a potential problem with opioid use is defined as a positive urine test for opioid(s) inconsistent with those disclosed by the participant during collection of concomitant medications, i.e., cannot be attributed to a reported prescribed opioid medication.

    24\. Has any medical condition\*, \*\* that, in the site investigator's judgment, poses a safety risk or interferes with the ability to adequately assess clinical trial endpoints.
  * Medical conditions include, but are not limited to, concomitant use of an oral medication with a narrow therapeutic index in which absorption may be impacted by delayed gastric emptying; a medical condition that precludes participant from taking study product; an active unstable or progressive major mental health or neurologic condition including, severe developmental disabilities, new or untreated psychosis or schizophrenia, and new or untreated bipolar I disorder.

    * Of note, an abnormal vital sign alone is not exclusionary at screening. However, the abnormal vital sign may be indicative of an exclusionary medical condition as described above.
sponsor: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
